newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares relinquish gains to close lower.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares relinquish gains to close lower.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange dropped on profit-taking in a special "moorat" trading session to mark the start of Hindu New Year, brokers said.
Brokers said the absence of foreign institutional investors (FIIs) and domestic mutual funds was another dampening factor.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 4.13 points lower at 690.35.
"Activity was confined to very few counters as investors booked profits even at low levels in the absence of any institutional buying," said Sumit Gandhi of brokers Rare Financial services.
Moorat trade is held on the festival day of Diwali to mark the start of the Hindu New year.
Reliance Industries dropped 2.10 rupees to 183.90, while TISCO fell 0.70 rupee to 167.0.
State Bank of India slipped 1.70 rupee to 217.90 and ITC fell 0.95 rupee to 255.10.
Larsen and Toubro remained unchanged at the previous close of 221.25 rupees.
The Delhi Stock Exchange will remain closed on Monday and Tuesday on account of Hindu festivals, officials said.
